verdict.rationale: Pylon's Connectors give its agents access to external tools. The connectors doc frames Custom API tools as the fallback for when a system does not provide an MCP server, which implies MCP servers can be plugged in as connectors. However, the evidence never explicitly describes adding an MCP server, its configuration, transport or auth, or which agents can use it. The Pylon MCP Server evidence is server-side and is not credited here. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of adding arbitrary or custom MCP servers, configuration and auth details, the supported list or scope of MCP connectors, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug MCP servers into this product so it can use their tools

citations.quote: If a system does not provide an MCP server, an administrator can define a Custom API tool that agents can use to hit internal or third party API endpoints.
Connectors give Pylon agents access to external tools so they can search for context, retrieve information, and take action outside Pylon.
